messages:
danielle: Heads-up 10: AcmeFinancial POC wants to upload a CSV of support tickets (names, emails, limited account IDs). Security asked whether that POC data makes the trial account fall into our ISO/ISMS scope. cc @sam @oliver

sam: short: yes if it's real customer data processed on our hosted trial it becomes in-scope for data controls (encryption, retention, access reviews). If they scrub/anonymize first it can be treated as out-of-scope. Need to know where data will live (hosted vs dedicated).

odr: typo? meant @oliver :)

oliver: For clarity: Hosted trial = Redwood-managed infra + keys. We do not provide customer-managed KMS for hosted. If customer requires BYOK or VPC isolation, recommend Dedicated or Private offering. Hosted can accept POC data only under explicit DPA + documented retention.

danielle: They asked if we can "guarantee" deletion after 30 days and provide an applicability statement for the SOW. Also want a short control mapping for encryption and key rotation to share with their security team.

sam: Deletion: operationally we can implement a 30-day retention TTL for POC accounts and remove logs on request, but we need this in writing in the DPA/SOW and an ops ticket to run the purge. We cannot promise customer-managed keys on hosted.

oliver: Here's a concise SOW snippet you can paste:

```
Applicability: Redwood Inference's ISMS (ISO 27001) applies to customer data processed within Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted trial accounts process data on Redwood-managed infrastructure and are not eligible for customer-managed key integrations by default. For any POC that ingests customer-identifiable information into a hosted trial, the following must be completed prior to ingestion: (1) a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA) referencing retention and deletion obligations; (2) a documented retention window (e.g., 30 days) enforced by Redwood; (3) confirmation of minimized dataset scope. For BYOK or VPC isolation, customer must use Dedicated or Private deployment options.
```

danielle: Perfect. Can we share a high-level control mapping now or do we need formal evidence/NDA?

oliver: We can share non-sensitive, high-level mappings publicly: AES-256 encryption at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit; Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS for hosted; CMK support for Private deployments; key rotation procedures and audit logs available. For formal ISO evidence (statements of applicability, control test results) we need an NDAs/legal request and will share via secure portal.

sam: quick bullets you can send to their sec team: - Encryption at rest: AES-256 S3/EBS/KMS wrapped keys - In transit: TLS 1.2+/1.3 - Key ownership: Hosted=Redwood KMS; Private=customer CMK supported - Rotation: annual rotation + emergency rotation playbook; access logged in CloudTrail - Retention: configurable per-account for POCs; documented purge workflow (ops ticket + verification)

sec-bot: Reminder: do not post system evidence or screenshots in public channels. Use secure-share or SRM for handing over ISO artifacts.

danielle: I'll send the SOW snippet + bullets and ask them to sign the DPA before any data ingestion. Looping legal for NDA/evidence pack. Thanks y'all :pray:
